correctness.rationale: For q=gamma*beta,c=epsilon*alpha/eta, positive-root relation yields nu K=c xstar+phi and q xstar(K-1)=mu. Direct substitution cancels larval fluxes and produces the strictly negative adult saturation term. A positive periodic orbit or compactly supported invariant probability gives average Wprime=0 and E[J]>0; no unweighted mean claim follows. Since xprime<=x(1+sigma*alpha-x), limsup x<=M; for M<xstar, Wprime<=-delta W eventually, and y,z decay exponentially. Plant logistic perturbation then forces x→1. Source RESULT.md step 5 gives an exact positive equilibrium with x decreasing to xstar as sigma varies. Independent checker symbolically cancels Wprime and confirms exact rational state; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: A stage-structured pollination model naturally asks which mean plant resource can support recurrent insects and when resources globally exclude them. The weighted mass law supplies a new quantitative necessary resource floor on cycles and a global, initial-biomass-independent sufficient extinction test, avoiding unjustified inference from local invasion threshold.

final_claim: For the exact deterministic PLA ODE with strictly positive plant and nonnegative insect stages, root xstar of qxstar(cxstar+phi)=nu(mu+qxstar) and K=1+mu/(qxstar) give W=y+Kz, Wprime=(x-xstar)(mu*y/xstar+cz)-cxz²/(eta+z). Every compact strictly positive invariant law satisfies E[xA]/E[A]>xstar; if 1+sigma*alpha<xstar all insects become exponentially extinct and x tends to one.
limitations: Only the stated autonomous homogeneous PLA ODE, positive parameter range, and compact interior invariant laws; neither actual periodic-orbit existence nor necessary extinction threshold proved.
